issues.description: Guard predicate `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` is too broad and fires for every non-Tab key, not just Enter/Return.
issues.detail: The new branch dismisses the popup and re-dispatches the event for arrow keys, Escape, Backspace, modifiers, and more. The intended precondition is `key in (Return, Enter)`. As written, the contract of keyPressEvent is silently widened and dismissal/navigation keys route through a path meant for accept-keys.

issues.description: Manually re-dispatching the event via `textedit.keyPressEvent(event)` leaks the editor's event pipeline into the popup.
issues.detail: Calling the parent editor's handler directly bypasses Qt's normal propagation, couples the completion widget to textedit internals, and skips any focus/proxy logic Qt may insert. Prefer `event.ignore()` (plus `hide()`) and let Qt route the key naturally.

issues.description: Special-case bolted into an already-busy keyPressEvent rather than restructuring the key dispatch.
issues.detail: The new branch is spliced ahead of the existing `item is None` guard and overlaps the downstream Enter/Return/Tab accept block, so the Enter path is not cleanly short-circuited. Compute once at the top whether the key is an accept key (based on config + key) and let the rest of the handler stay unchanged.

issues.description: No test or written specification for the new option's behavioral contract.
issues.detail: The PR ships a behavioral switch without an automated test exercising either branch and without stating which keys accept, dismiss, or navigate under each setting. A single test toggling the pref off, sending Enter, and asserting no acceptance would prevent silent regression and document the contract for subclasses.

issues.description: `get_conf` is called on every keystroke for a static user preference.
issues.detail: A config dictionary walk on the hot path of typing inside the completion popup is wasteful. Cache the value when the popup is shown or subscribe to config changes so the predicate is a cheap attribute read.

issues.description: Style: `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` should be `key != Qt.Key_Tab`.
issues.detail: The `not x == y` form is a code-review tell that the author was transcribing rather than reasoning about the expression. Trivial fix that matches surrounding code voice and removes reliance on operator-precedence folklore.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the patch addresses a real user problem but needs work before landing. The core defect is a guard predicate that fires for every non-Tab key — including Escape, arrows, and modifiers — combined with a cross-widget re-dispatch into `textedit.keyPressEvent` that leaks the editor's event pipeline into the popup. The branch is also spliced into an already-overloaded keyPressEvent rather than restructured as a top-level "is this an accept key?" predicate, leaving the downstream Enter path not cleanly short-circuited. Secondary concerns: no test, per-keystroke `get_conf` calls, and a `not x == y` style smell. Fix the predicate to Enter/Return only, replace manual forwarding with `event.ignore()`, cache the config value, and add one regression test.
